story.titleZh: 法拉利奥斯汀再失杆位 轮胎升温短板依旧
story.summaryZh: 法拉利在奥斯汀未能夺得杆位，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿分列第四、第五，勒克莱尔认为轮胎升温窗口和Q3气温下降是主要原因。
story.originalTitle: Why another Ferrari pole bid faltered
story.summaryEn: Ferrari missed out on pole position in Austin, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton finishing fourth and fifth, and Leclerc pointed to tyre warm-up and a drop in temperature in Q3 as the main reasons.
detailZh: 周五练习赛最快车队法拉利在2026年第18次未能夺得大奖赛杆位，这次是在奥斯汀，原因是两个熟悉的弱点和不利的时机。
夏尔·勒克莱尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿最终位列第四和第五，但两人对于为何无法匹敌基米·安东内利的梅赛德斯和两辆红牛略有不同看法。
今年的法拉利一直受困于单圈轮胎弱点，这使它在全年大部分时间里周六弱于周日。
“这非常令人失望，因为我认为有些周末我们在自由练习中很强，但到了排位赛，很明显其他人在直道上快得多，我们很难匹配，”周五最快车手勒克莱尔说。
“但我觉得这是一场我们赛车有潜力的排位赛，不过赛车也包括轮胎，而在Q3中，不幸的是，我们没能处在正确的位置。”
“Q3时温度大概低了1°C或2°C，对我来说，这是巨大的差别。出场圈就真的很挣扎。”
“从出场圈开始我就滑动得相当厉害，这让之后变得非常困难。”
勒克莱尔呼吁法拉利“更加努力，尝试非常透彻地理解这些轮胎，甚至比我们现在做得更好，因为我认为其他人通常拥有更多一点”。
他说：“他们在第三节排位赛中提取圈速比我们容易一些。一旦我们稍微偏离窗口，就会付出很大代价。所以这是我们需要研究的问题。”
尽管进行了多次升级，这仍然是法拉利全年的一大特征，因此这引出了一个问题：这是否是赛车理念中固有的东西，直到2027年才能解决。
当The Race向勒克莱尔提出这一理论时，他说：“不，我不会这么说，但这可能是你必须在正赛和排位赛之间做出选择的一种妥协。”
同样的弱点导致它在排位赛中难以让轮胎保持在正确窗口，但在正赛中却是保护轮胎的优势。
这就是为什么勒克莱尔预计周日的情况会更好，就像在斯帕等赛道上那样，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在排位赛获得第五和第六名后，正赛分别以第二和第四名完赛。
至于汉密尔顿，他并不觉得轮胎温度是个问题。“我的出场圈非常好，所以对我来说没有问题。赛车感觉很好，那一圈很干净。真的完全没有问题，”他说。
相反，他将法拉利的主要弱点归结为差距的原因。
法拉利在2026年最大的单一弱点一直是其动力单元，这在奥斯汀再次让他们付出了代价，尤其是在长长的后直道上。
汉密尔顿在排位赛中获得第五名后感到意外，得知自己的名次后，他对比赛工程师卡洛·桑蒂说：“这些家伙在Q3最后一圈肯定提速了，因为那段时间去哪了？”
但数据并未显示太多这方面的证据，因为法拉利在所有三个阶段排位赛中的直线速度劣势是一致的。实际上，勒克莱尔在后直道末端比汉密尔顿慢5公里/小时，比安东内利慢10公里/小时。
汉密尔顿（绿线）在到达后直道时比安东内利（基准线）快近十分之一秒——事实上在那个时间点汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔净排名是1-2——但到后直道末端时，汉密尔顿落后多达十分之二秒。
“我们的赛车非常扎实，也许比其他人稍好一些，”汉密尔顿说。
“但我认为他们在底盘方面已经追近了。我们看到红牛在降低阻力方面追近了。梅赛德斯至少带来了零点三秒的升级。我认为他们开始弄清楚如何利用这一点了。”
“所以他们在弯道中现在与我们匹敌。我们无法在本赛季迈出那一步，在直道上缩小那速度差距。”
当被问及红牛在直道上的相对速度时，汉密尔顿说：“有些地方是零点三到零点五秒。也许是零点四秒。这相当令人印象深刻。我不知道你们有没有看过叠加图——进入1号弯时，我们的速度开始下降，而他们的速度则继续保持。”
“所以这很难与之竞争。如果我们拥有和他们相同的动力，我们就会直接参与战斗。我认为我们很可能能进入头排。”
“但我们知道情况就是这样，所以我们会尽量加以利用。”
汉密尔顿0.276秒的差距中有一部分曾被短暂追回，但他最终在最后一个弯出弯时出现了小失误，这让他失去了击败勒克莱尔的机会，甚至可能错失插入两辆红牛之间的机会。
时机不巧？
勒克莱尔在Q3的圈速实际上比他在Q2的最佳成绩还要慢，如果重复那一圈，他本可以排在基米·安东内利旁边占据头排发车位。
勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿实际上是仅有的两位在Q3中合法提升成绩的车手，他们的圈速优于其他任何人的最后一搏。不幸的是，对法拉利而言，安东内利和红牛车手在Q3首轮冲刺中已做出更快圈速。
哈贾尔：1分34.363秒（因超出赛道限制被删除）
诺里斯：1分34.379秒（因超出赛道限制被删除）
维斯塔潘：1分34.482秒（因超出赛道限制被删除）
看起来，法拉利确实是在赛道条件相比梅赛德斯/红牛显得更不利时做出了Q3最快圈，当时风力更大、云层更厚，且出现在本节稍晚阶段。
最终，它可能为未能在后来被证明至关重要的Q3首轮跑中同样出色地执行而付出了代价，当时它仅列第四和第六。
detailEn: Friday Formula 1 pacesetter Ferrari fell short of a grand prix pole position for the 18th time in 2026, this time at Austin, because of two familiar weaknesses and unfortunate timing.
Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton ended up fourth and fifth but had slightly different views on why they could not match Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes and the two Red Bulls.
This year's Ferrari has battled a single-lap tyre weakness that has left it weaker on Saturdays than Sundays for much of the year.

"It's very disappointing because I think there are some other weekends where we've been strong in free practice, but then come quali, it's very clear that the others are just having a lot more in the straights, and it's very difficult for us to match that," Friday pacesetter Leclerc said.
"But I felt like it's a qualifying where we had the potential in the car, but the car also includes tyres, and in Q3, unfortunately, we were not in the right place.
"It was like 1°C or 2°C less in Q3, and for me, it was a huge difference. Just really struggled in the outlap.
"I was sliding quite a lot already from the outlap, and that made it very difficult after that."
Leclerc called on Ferrari to "work harder and try and understand those tyres very well, even better than what we are doing now, because the others I think normally have a bit more".

"It's a bit easier for them to extract the laptime in Q3 than it is for us," he said. "As soon as we are a tiny bit outside the window, we pay the price a lot. So this is something that we need to look into."

It has been a characteristic of the Ferrari throughout the year despite multiple upgrades, so that raises the question of whether it is something intrinsic to the car philosophy that can't be fixed until 2027.
"No, I wouldn't say that, but it's maybe a bit of a compromise that you would have to choose between race and qualifying," Leclerc said when The Race put that theory to him.
The same weakness that leaves it struggling to keep its tyres in the right window in qualifying is a tyre preservation strength in the races.
It's why Leclerc expected things to be better on Sunday, as was the case at races such as Spa, where Leclerc and Hamilton finished second and fourth after qualifying fifth and sixth.
As for Hamilton, he didn't feel tyre temperature was an issue. "I had a really good out lap, so no problems for me. The car felt good, it was a clean lap. No issues at all, really," he said.
Instead, he zeroed in on Ferrari's main weakness as the cause of the deficit.
Ferrari's single-biggest weakness in 2026 has been its power unit and that cost it once again at Austin, in particular down the long back straight.

Hamilton was caught off guard by qualifying fifth and after being informed of his position, he told his race engineer Carlo Santi: "These guys must be turning it up for that last Q3, because where did that time go?"

But the data did not show much evidence of that as Ferrari's straightline deficit is consistent throughout all three stages of qualifying. Leclerc is actually 5km/h down on Hamilton at the end of the back straight, and 10km/h down on Antonelli.

Hamilton (green line) is almost a tenth up on Antonelli (baseline) as they reach the back straight - in fact Hamilton and Leclerc are a net 1-2 at that snapshot in time - but by the time they're at the end of it Hamilton slipped as far as two tenths back.
"Our car is really solid, maybe slightly better than the others," Hamilton said.

"But I think they have closed up on chassis. We've seen the Red Bull close up on their downforce. Mercedes took a three-tenths step of upgrade, at least. I think they're starting to figure out how to utilise that.
"So they're now matching us through the corners. We're not able to take that step in this season to close that speed on the straight."

Asked about the comparative straightline speed of the Red Bull, Hamilton said: "Some places it's three to five tenths. Maybe it's four tenths. It's pretty impressive. I don't know if you've seen the overlays - Into Turn 1, ours starts dipping and theirs just keeps going.
"So that's hard to compete with. If we had the same power as them, we would be right there in the battle. I think we could probably be on the front row.
"But we know that's the case, so we try to make the most of it."

Some of Hamilton's 0.276s deficit was briefly reclaimed, but Hamilton ended up making a small error out of the final corner that cost him the chance of beating Leclerc and potentially even splitting the Red Bulls.
Unfortunate timing?
Leclerc's Q3 lap was actually slower than his best Q2 effort, which, if repeated, would have put him on the front row alongside Kimi Antonelli.

Leclerc and Hamilton were actually the only two drivers to legally improve on their Q3 run with laptimes better than anyone else's final efforts. Unfortunately for Ferrari, Antonelli and the Red Bulls had set better laps on their first Q3 runs.
Hadjar: 1m34.363s (track limits deleted)
Norris: 1m34.379s (track limits deleted)
Verstappen: 1m34.482s (track limits deleted)

It does appear the Ferraris set their fastest Q3 laps when the track conditions looked less favourable compared to the Mercedes/Red Bulls, with gustier winds and more cloud cover later in the session.
Ultimately, it may have paid the price for not executing as well on what turned out to be crucial first Q3 runs, where it was fourth and sixth.
keyPointsZh: 这是法拉利2026年第18次未能夺得大奖赛杆位。
勒克莱尔称Q3气温比之前低约1至2摄氏度，他在出场圈就打滑严重。
keyPointsEn: This was the 18th time in 2026 that Ferrari failed to take a grand prix pole position.
Leclerc said Q3 was about 1-2°C cooler and that he was already sliding a lot on the outlap.

relatedItems.titleZh: F1在美国仍‘非常小’ - 多门纳利
relatedItems.summaryZh: 尽管近年来F1在美国地区增长巨大，但F1首席执行官斯蒂法诺·多门纳利认为该赛事在美国仍然‘非常小’。多门纳利在接受The Race联合创始人Darren Cox采访时表示，尽管F1在美国的粉丝数量已达5200万，但与其它美国体育相比，仍有巨大的潜力待挖掘。
relatedItems.originalTitle: F1 still 'very small' in US - Domenicali
detailZh: 一级方程式首席执行官斯蒂法诺·多梅尼卡利认为，尽管近年来该地区取得了巨大增长，但锦标赛在美国仍然“非常小”。
多梅尼卡利在接受《赛车》联合创始人达伦·科克斯采访时表示，这次采访是在Axios和《赛车》的《超越赛车：创新与领导力投资》活动上进行的，该活动在拉斯维加斯举行，是F1赛历上的三场美国赛事之一。
当自由媒体公司在2017年完成对F1的收购时，美国只有一场赛事，美国人对其他主要市场的兴趣落后。
但现在，根据F1自己的数据，截至去年年底，美国有5200万粉丝，比前一年增长了11%，与十年前的情况完全不同。
F1还与美国苹果公司签订了为期五年的合作协议，成为其新的美国广播合作伙伴，该公司表示，这在上个月已经使观众数量同比增长了13%——尽管对其影响存在争议。美国球迷也能在Netflix上通过特别流媒体合作观看今年的加拿大大奖赛。
尽管有这种多方面的增长，但多门卡利仍然觉得与美国的其他运动相比，还有很多未被挖掘的潜力。
“今天我对我的团队说，我们在美国很小，但我们正在以相当高的速度增长，”多门卡利在Axios和《赛车》联合创始人Darren Cox以及《赛车》的《超越赛车：创新与领导力投资》活动中告诉Darren Cox。
“但当我们每天醒来，除了你已有的新闻外，还有F1的新闻，还有你对NFL、NBA以及其他这个国家热爱的所有运动的兴趣，因为它是文化的一部分。它是你与生俱来的感性的一部分。”
“我们需要进入学校，我们需要进入大学，因为幕后，那些了解这项运动的人都知道，有一个不可思议的机会来谈论技术，谈论这项运动的复杂性水平。”
“我们的重点是吸引人们，谈论我们作为一项运动，作为一个行业。我在谈论行业，因为每个车队背后都有一个不可思议的供应链阵容，一个令人难以置信的技术阵容，每个人都想参与其中。”
“所以对我们来说，有如此多的角度来吸引人们的兴趣。这很迷人。我敢说没有多少平台能做这件事。”
“因此，这是我们需要通过合作伙伴的协作不断确保的事情：无论出于什么原因吸引每个人，但随后进入了解我们是谁的知识，因为这是基础，为了可信，为了长期吸引那些可能是因为与我们的运动无关的兴趣而进入的人。”
Netflix的《生存之战》也对F1在美国的增长起到了关键作用。
当时，由于Covid疫情，人们需要通过电脑或电视等设备保持联系，[《生存之战》]在那些我们当时没有机会如此相关的市场中，对于提高我们对体育运动的认知起到了至关重要的作用，”多梅尼卡利补充道。
自由时代与伯尼·埃克莱斯顿领导下的旧F1运营模式有着重大的区别。
多梅尼卡利赞扬了埃克莱斯顿如何将F1发展壮大，但同时也指出了他一直致力于让F1摆脱的排他性问题。
“在过去几年里，一级方程式赛车从以前的样子到现在的样子，确实有很大的不同，”多梅尼卡利说
“在伯尼·埃克莱斯顿的领导下，采取那样的策略绝对是正确的：去创造原本不存在的东西。去建立一个对技术充满热情、对赛车充满热情、对环游世界充满热情的社区。
“但这个社区只是专注于赛车运动，仅此而已。带有排他性的负面含义。在排他性的意义上：第一个回答是‘不’，而不是‘是的，如何？’。在自由媒体控制权变更之后，如果我们想要保持相关性，我们就必须采取不同的范式。
“很多人……生活是美好的，因为空中充满了许多话语，但很多人都在书写。很多人认为我们的运动几年前就死了。这对那些热爱竞争、在赛道上比赛的人来说是一个巨大的机会，去展示当时人们所说的话。当然，并不是所有人。他们是错的。
“但简单来说，我们认为这是一个很好的机会让我们变得相关，因为我们认为我们拥有所有成为真正优秀的元素，在保持运动成为我们策略中心的同时，尝试随着社交媒体内容的发展而发展。”
“确保参与是由我们的英雄们，车手们，车队们，人们来完成的。解释幕后的情况。尝试给真正的铁杆粉丝一个谈论运动的机会，同时利用我们的平台与那些对运动一无所知的人群建立联系。”
“这就是我们现在在这个方面变得相关的理由，因为一级方程式赛车为那些相信我们的合作伙伴提供了一个机会去做他们认为对他们有利的事情。”
“我必须说，今天我们收到的最大的赞美是：‘一级方程式赛车是你要去的地方’。当你这么说的时候，那意味着很大的事情。”
detailEn: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali believes the championship is still “very small in the US” despite its huge growth in the region in recent years.

Domenicali was speaking to The Race co-founder Darren Cox at Axios and The Race’s Beyond the Race: Investments in Innovation and Leadership event in Las Vegas - one of three US races on the F1 calendar.
When Liberty Media completed its takeover of F1 in 2017, there was only one US race and American interest was lagging behind other key markets.
But now, according to F1’s own figures, it had 52 million fans in the United States as of the end of last year, an 11% increase on the year before and a totally different picture to a decade ago.

F1 also struck a five-year deal with Apple as its new broadcast partner in the US too, something it said back in August had increased viewership 13% year on year - even if there’s debate around its impact. US fans were also able to watch this year’s Canadian Grand Prix on Netflix in a special streaming collaboration.
But despite that multi-pronged growth, Domenicali still feels there’s lots of untapped potential compared to other sports in the US.

“Today I said to my people, we are very small in the US, but we are growing at quite a high speed,” Domenicali told The Race co-founder Darren Cox at Axios and The Race’s Beyond the Race: Investments in Innovation and Leadership event.

“But we’re going to crush the market when, every day when you wake up, you have the news of Formula 1, on top of the news that you have, on top of the interest in the NFL, the NBA, in all the other sports that the country loves, because it’s part of the culture. It’s part of the sensibility that you were born with.

“We need to get into the schools, we need to get into the universities, because behind the scenes, and the ones that know this sport know very well, there is an incredible opportunity to talk about technology, talking about the level of complexity of this sport.

“Our focus is to attract people and talk about us as a sport, as an industry. I’m talking about the industry, because behind every team there is an incredible line-up of supply chains, a line-up of incredible technology, that everyone wants to be involved in.
“So for us, there are so many angles to attract the interest of people. It’s fascinating. And I would say there are not so many platforms that can do that.

“Therefore this is something that, through the collaboration of our partners, we need to keep making sure: that everyone is attracted for whatever reason, but then goes into the knowledge of who we are, because that’s fundamental, to be credible, and to stay long-term attractive to the people, who maybe came in because of an interest that was not really related to our sport specifically.”
Netflix’s Drive To Survive has also been key to F1’s growth in the US.

“At that time, when there was Covid, when people needed to be connected to a computer or TV or whatever it was, [Drive To Survive] was instrumental in growing the awareness of the sport in markets where we didn’t have the chance to be so relevant at that time,” Domenicali added.
The Liberty era has been a monumental departure from how F1 was run under the old Bernie Ecclestone-fronted regime.
Domenicali paid tribute to how Ecclestone was able to build F1 up but highlighted an exclusivity problem that he’s been very keen to pull F1 away from.
“The evolution of what Formula 1 was before and what Formula 1 is now, in the last couple of years, is definitely different,” Domenicali said

“It was absolutely the right strategy, under the leadership of Bernie Ecclestone, to do what he did: to build something that was not there. To build a community that was passionate about technology, passionate about racing, passionate about travelling around the world.

“But it was a community that was just focused on motorsport, full stop. With a negative term of exclusivity. Exclusivity in terms of: the first answer was ‘no’, instead of ‘yes, and how?’. And under the Liberty change of control, we had to do a different paradigm if we wanted to be relevant.

“A lot of people... and life is beautiful because a lot of words can fly around the air, but a lot of people wrote it. A lot of people thought that our sport was dead, not so many years ago. That is an incredible opportunity for the people that are racing inside, who love the competition, to show what the people were saying at that time. Not everyone, of course. They were wrong.

“But in simple terms, the reason why we thought it was a great opportunity for us to be relevant is because we thought that we have all the elements to be really good, in terms of keeping the sport at the centre of our strategy, but trying to evolve with the social media content.

“Trying to make sure that the engagement was done by our heroes, the drivers, the teams, the people. Explaining what is behind the scenes. Trying to give the opportunity not only to the real hardcore fans to talk about the sport, but using our platform to connect with an audience that didn’t know anything about the sport.
“That’s the reason why now we are relevant in that respect, because F1 is giving an opportunity for the partners who believe in us to do what they believe is right for their interest.
“And I have to say, today the biggest compliment that we receive is: ‘Formula 1 is the place to be’. When you say that, it’s something big.”

多门纳利认为F1在美国仍有巨大的市场潜力待挖掘。

Domenicali feels there is a lot of untapped potential in the US market for F1.

relatedItems.summaryZh: F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利解释了为何提前推进V8引擎回归，称当初影响2026规则制定的“生存”之争已不再需要。F1与FIA周五宣布一致同意V8新规于2030年启用，比原定2031年提前一年。
relatedItems.originalTitle: 'We are not stupid people' - Domenicali on why F1 is going back to V8s
relatedItems.summaryEn: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has explained why the return to V8 engines has been fast-tracked, saying the fight to "survive" that shaped the 2026 rules is no longer needed. F1 and the FIA announced on Friday unanimous agreement for new V8 regulations to take effect in 2030, one year earlier than the original 2031 timeframe.
detailZh: F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利解释了为何V8引擎回归被提前推进，称当初影响2026规则制定的“生存”之争已不再需要。
当前的50/50涡轮混合动力单元尚未完成首个赛季的比赛，但F1与FIA于周五宣布，各方一致同意新的V8规则于2030年生效。
这一戏剧性的方向转变，尽管多梅尼卡利此前曾强力捍卫现行规则——这些规则因让赛车能量匮乏而在车迷中引发分歧。
这也比最初厂商与赛事利益相关方商定50/50规则时设定的2031年时间表提前了一年。
周五在拉斯维加斯举行的 Axios 与 The Race 联合活动“超越赛道：创新与领导力投资”上，多梅尼卡利向 The Race 联合创始人达伦·考克斯表示，他阐述了新引擎为何合理。
多梅尼卡利解释说，2026 年的规则实际上并非 F1 主动推动的事项。
相反，它们是必然之举，由两个因素共同触发——当时正值新冠疫情引发全球金融不确定性的时期，大奖赛管理层正在规划未来规则。
首先，当时制造商们寻求全面电动化的未来，多梅尼卡利表示，F1 反对完全依赖电池的立场意味着必须达成一种 50/50 的折中方案。
其次，在新冠疫情造成的经济冲击下，如果失去制造商，F1将面临重大风险，因此它并不处于强势地位，无法抵制制造商的要求。
正如多梅尼卡利所说：“有必要做我们现在正在做的事情，否则我们就不会有赛车了。就这么简单。
“所以这就是为什么管理起来要复杂得多。但这也正是美妙之处，因为这给了我们重新创造、尝试书写新故事（并）创造新关注点的可能性。”
在2020年底至2021年初有一段时间，红牛尚未完全承诺其引擎计划，雷诺在讨论该怎么做，奥迪尚未签约，在最坏的情况下，法拉利和梅赛德斯可能不得不被说服为所有车队供应引擎。
这可能是他们此前不愿做的事情，而那样做会让F1陷入危机局面。
这就是为什么对F1和FIA来说，制定规则让所有制造商满意、尤其是说服奥迪加入，被证明如此关键。
多梅尼卡利解释说，如今世界已大不相同，转向更便宜、更轻、更受欢迎的V8引擎是显而易见的选择——因为F1不再需要如此迁就汽车制造商的需求。
当被问及F1为何如此迅速地偏离现行规则时，多梅尼卡利表示：“很简单。因为我们希望与未来保持相关性。”
“我确实相信，我们之所以做出改变，是因为需要保持吸引力并与技术保持相关性。”
“当时，在与国际汽联、制造商或汽车行业的规则决策中，大家都想走电动化，而我们不想走电动化，就这样。”
“那么平衡点是什么？走向混合动力。所以是50比50，不管具体比例如何。我们知道那是当时生存下去的必要条件。”
“而且，我们不是愚蠢的人。因此我们与很多人进行了讨论：车手、车队、制造商。这种演变是自然而然的。”
尽管F1过去曾因陷入无休止的规则变更循环而受到批评——这些规则似乎从未获得足够时间稳固下来——但多梅尼卡利认为，原地踏步同样糟糕。
“我回到一点：不改变的运动正在失去机会，”他说。
当被问及反复修订规则可能阻碍F1的推广时，多梅尼卡利表示：“恰恰相反。阻碍在于一项不理解变革需求的运动。
“我的意思是，你需要有吸引力，并理解大众的走向。”
detailEn: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has explained why a return to V8 engines has been fast-tracked, with a fight to “survive” that influenced the 2026 rules no longer needed.

The current 50/50 turbo hybrid power units have yet to complete their first season of racing, but F1 and the FIA announced on Friday that there was unanimous agreement for new V8 regulations to come into play for 2030.
The dramatic change of direction comes despite Domenicali’s robust defence of the current regulations that have divided opinions among fans because of the way they have left cars so energy-starved.
It is also one year earlier than the 2031 timeframe that was laid down when the 50/50 rules were originally agreed between manufacturers and championship stakeholders.

Speaking to The Race co-founder Darren Cox at Axios and The Race’s Beyond the Race: Investments in Innovation and Leadership event in Las Vegas on Friday, Domenicali offered insight into why new engines make sense.
Domenicali explained that the 2026 regulations were not actually something that F1 had actively been pushing for.
Instead, they were a necessity triggered by two factors coming together as grand prix chiefs planned future rules amid the times of global financial uncertainty triggered by the Covid pandemic.
First, with manufacturers looking back then for an all-electric future, Domenicali says a pushback from F1 against going full battery meant a compromise 50/50 element had to be settled upon.
And secondly, amid the economic fallout of the Covid pandemic, F1 faced major risks if it lost manufacturers, so it was not in a position of strength to resist what they wanted.
As Domenicali said: “There was the need to do what we are doing now, because otherwise we would not have had the cars. Simple as that.

“So that’s why it’s a much more complicated exercise to manage. But that’s also the beauty, because this gives us the possibility of reinventing, trying to create a new story, [and] create new attention.”

There was a period in late 2020/early 2021, with Red Bull not yet fully committed to its engine plans, Renault debating what to do, and Audi not having signed up, that in a worst-case scenario Ferrari and Mercedes could have needed to be leaned on to supply all teams.
This is something they may not have been willing to do, which would have put F1 in a crisis situation.
This is why it proved so critical for F1 and the FIA to create rules that kept all manufacturers happy and especially convinced Audi to join.
Domenicali explained that, with the world in a different place now, moving to cheaper, lighter and more popular V8s was a no-brainer – as F1 did not need to kowtow to the needs of car makers so much.
Asked about why F1 was so quickly moving away from the current rules, Domenicali said: “Very simple. Because we want to be relevant for the future.
“I do believe that the reason why we are changing is because there is the need to be attractive and relevant to the technology.
“At that moment there was the decision on the regulations with the FIA, the manufacturers, or the automotive industry, wanted to be electric, and we didn’t want to go electric, full stop.
“So what is the balance? Going to be hybrid. So 50-50, whatever it is. And we knew that was a need to survive in that moment.
“And then, we are not stupid people. And therefore we were having discussions with a lot of people: drivers, teams, manufacturers. And the evolution is natural.”
While F1 has faced criticisms in the past for being in an endless cycle of rule changes that never seem to be given enough time to bed down, Domenicali thinks that standing still is just as bad.
“I go back to one thing: the sport that doesn’t change is losing opportunity,” he said.

Asked about repeated revisions of the regulations being a potential blocker of selling F1, Domenicali said: “It’s the other way around. The blocker is a sport that is not understanding the need for change.
“I mean, you need to be attractive and understand where the mass is going.”

relatedItems.titleZh: 拉斯维加斯排位赛中那场“疯狂”的牵引效果实际价值
relatedItems.summaryZh: 在拉斯维加斯的一级方程式排位赛中，车手安东内利通过其他车辆的牵引获得了关键优势，尽管他最终因罚分无法从杆位发车，但在排位赛中他是最快的。牵引效果如此强大，以至于他在最后一圈几乎与林德布拉德的小红牛车队赛车并驾齐驱，最终仅落后0.6秒。安东内利承认，如果没有牵引，他可能无法取得这样的成绩。

media.altZh: 拉斯维加斯排位赛中那场“疯狂”的牵引效果实际价值 · 第 1 张

relatedItems.originalTitle: What 'crazy' tow was actually worth in Vegas qualifying
detailZh: 在拉斯维加斯的F1排位赛中，从另一辆车中获得牵引至关重要，没有什么能像基米·安东内利的最佳圈速那样，展示出‘疯狂’的收益。
尽管安东内利由于赛道处罚无法从杆位发车，但在排位赛中他是最快的，尽管他‘对赛车没有感觉’并且Q3阶段的最后一圈比预想的更接近阿维德·林德布拉德的小红牛车队。
然而，牵引效果如此强大，安东内利在林德布拉德启动圈速内两秒处起步，最终仅落后0.6秒，并在两条最长的直道上获得了惊人的尾流。
他从中受益是显而易见的，安东内利也迅速承认了这一点：‘我以为我完蛋了，但这里的牵引太强大了，我能够仅仅通过它来提升成绩。’
然而，他从麦拉伦车队老板安德烈亚·斯特拉所说的“一个非常极端的案例”中获得的程度令人印象深刻。
牵引和没有牵引之间的差异很大，从0.5-1.0秒不等，具体取决于你比较的是谁的圈速。奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂甚至说“如果你没有做到这一点，你甚至都不用出去”。
维斯塔潘和拉塞尔在Q3的各自最佳圈速中，从领先他们三秒多的车辆那里获得了轻微的牵引，而兰多·诺里斯在跑出比队友皮亚斯蒂快两秒的圈速时，也得到了很好的牵引。
但没有人能接近安东内利。当他通过整个赛道逼近林德布拉德时，安东内利在所有四个直道上都获得了强大的牵引和直线速度优势。
这是一个他本不应该出现在的地方，如果不是因为他明智地退出了混乱的多车追逐战，争夺赛道位置。
这使安东内利在计时器耗尽之前开始最后一圈的时间紧迫，也意味着他的轮胎准备受到了影响，但这种方式给了他意想不到的巨大回报。他主动出击，掌控了自己的局势，显然也有些运气在他得到回报的时候。
当所有九辆车在最后一节Q3的比赛中几乎同时开始他们的圈数，安东内利排在最后——在赛道上，安东内利在Strip上大约有四辆车，每多一辆车在队列中都会带来一点额外的牵引力，这超出了林德布拉德的主要尾流。
“牵引力是疯狂的，”领先安东内利的驾驶员皮埃尔·加斯利说。
“如果你看看安东内利的最后一段，你就明白有多强大。我从未在任何一辆车上感受过这样的力量。”
不出所料，安东内利在每一段直道上都比前四名快了0.9-1.4秒，但同时在每个弯道部分也是最慢的，刹车最早，最低速度慢了几公里每小时，总共损失了大约0.6-1.0秒在污染的空气中。
与图表上的其他三人相比，他在The Strip上就比他们快了半秒以上，然后在16号弯到终点线的跑道上快了0.2-0.5秒（诺里斯的麦克拉伦在这里直道上特别慢，比安东内利慢20公里每小时）。
他的最高速度优势由于每个人的引擎开始超级剪切并即使在全油门下也减速而略有减弱。
这就是安东内利说自己是“仅靠最后一段赛道”才取得最快成绩的原因——这比队友乔治·拉塞尔的最佳成绩快了0.480秒，比马克斯·维斯塔潘最快的第三段赛道快了0.908秒。
这超过了安东内利在第一、二段赛道上比维斯塔潘和兰多·诺里斯慢了大约六十分之一秒的劣势，在那里红牛和麦克拉伦比奔驰车队都快。
维斯塔潘表示“在直线上的速度提升简直疯狂”并且说“我在Q3的第一圈几乎已经是最快了”——这简直不是被拖车辅助的安东内利的对手。尽管安东内利在通过弯道时在脏空气中行驶的负面影响方面做得很好，但这个布局在这一年中可以说是最友好的了。
这本来可能是一个安东内利只排在第四快的排位赛，如果一切正常进行的话。然而，正如他所说：“那是一种你认为你完蛋了，但实际上却成功了的情况。”
detailEn: Getting a tow from another car was absolutely critical in Formula 1 qualifying in Las Vegas, with nothing demonstrating how “crazy” the gain could be like Kimi Antonelli’s session-topping lap.

Though Antonelli will not actually start from pole due to a grid penalty, he was fastest in qualifying despite having “zero feeling with the car” and spending most of his final lap in Q3 much closer than intended to Arvid Lindblad’s Racing Bulls.

So powerful was the tow effect, though, that Antonelli benefitted significantly overall by starting the lap within two seconds of Lindblad, finishing it barely 0.6s behind and getting a stunning slipstream down the two longest straights.
That he benefited was obvious, and Antonelli was swift to acknowledge it: “I thought I was screwed but the tow is so big here that I was able to just gain with that.”
However, the full extent of how he gained from what McLaren team boss Andrea Stella called a "really extreme case" of slipstreaming was remarkable to see.
The difference between a tow and no tow was vast, anywhere from 0.5-1.0s depending on whose laps you compare. Oscar Piastri even said “you might as well not even go out if you don't get that right”.

Verstappen and Russell were picking up slight tows from cars just over three seconds ahead on their respective best laps in Q3, while Lando Norris had a good tow from running within two seconds of team-mate Piastri on his fastest.
But none of them came close to Antonelli. As he closed on Lindblad through the lap, Antonelli ended up with a strong tow and straightline speed advantage on all four straights.
It was a place he would not have been in had he not had the good sense to back out of a messy, multi-car fight for track position on his outlap.

That did put Antonelli in a race against time to start his final lap before the timer ran out on the session, and meant his tyre preparation was compromised, but it paid him back big time in a way Antonelli had not intended. He was proactive, took control of his situation, and there was obviously some fortune in how he was then rewarded.

As all nine cars on their final Q3 runs started their laps within 17s of each other, and Antonelli was last in the queue – on the Strip Antonelli had four cars within about six seconds, and each extra car in the queue added a little more of a tow benefit on top of the primary slipstream from Lindblad.
“The tow was insane,” said Pierre Gasly, who was one of the drivers ahead of Antonelli.
“If you look at the last sector of Antonelli, you just understand how powerful. I've never, ever felt that in a car.”

Unsurprisingly, Antonelli was the quickest of the top four on every straight by an overall gain of 0.9-1.4s depending on the comparison, but the slowest through every corner section at the same time, braking earliest and running a few km/h slower minimum speed totalling a loss of around 0.6-1.0s in the dirty air.

He seemed to gain over half a second down The Strip alone compared to the other three on the graph above, then between 0.2s and 0.5s on the run out of Turn 16 to the finish line (Norris’s McLaren being particularly slow on the straight here and 20km/h down on Antonelli).
His sheer top speed advantage was augmented by a slightly reduced effect as everyone’s engines began superclipping and slowing down even while on full throttle.

That’s why Antonelli said qualifying fastest was “only thanks to the final sector” – which was 0.480s quicker than team-mate George Russell’s best and a mammoth 0.908s clear of Max Verstappen’s fastest sector three.
This more than offset the six tenths or so Antonelli lost to Verstappen and Lando Norris in the first two sectors, where the Red Bull and McLaren were faster than both Mercedes.

Verstappen said “it's just insane how much you gain on the straights” and that “my first lap in Q3 was pretty much as good as it can be” – it was just no match for a tow-assisted Antonelli. And though Antonelli did a good job to mitigate the negative effect of running in dirty air through the corners, this layout is about as friendly to that as any could be all year.

This could easily have been a qualifying session in which Antonelli was only fourth-fastest had it played out normally. Instead, as he said: “It was just one of those times where you think you're screwed, but actually it works out.”
keyPointsZh: 安东内利在排位赛中通过牵引获得了显著优势。
尽管因罚分无法从杆位发车，他在排位赛中仍然是最快的。
牵引效果在排位赛中至关重要，可以缩短0.5-1.0秒的差距。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli gained a significant advantage in the qualifying session through towing.
Despite a grid penalty, he was the fastest in the qualifying session.
The effect of towing in the qualifying session can reduce the gap by 0.5-1.0 seconds.
